transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-25 14:30 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Lena (CSM), Jamie (Altaeus Head of ML), Samir (Platform), Olivia (Security), Dana (Prod PM)
Shared artifacts: POC runbook (draft link), example token histogram (customer), Redwood benchmark spreadsheet (we'll share)

Summary:
Short call to align on POC activation sequence, confirm access gating, finalize success criteria (quality + perf + cost), and set milestones: kickoff, initial baseline bench, mid-point review, and exec readout. Focus on access windows (VPC / VPN), data handling constraints, and the key metric set.

Topics covered:
- Workload sizing and token distribution
- Baseline benchmarks and acceptance thresholds
- Access steps: VPC peering, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Timeline: kickoff -> smoke tests -> baseline -> mid-point -> exec readout
- Risks and rollback/fallback strategies (hosted vs dedicated)

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got a solid agenda — want to make sure by the end of this call we have dates for kickoff and the exec readout plus owners for access. Uh, quick intros?
[00:12] Jamie: Hi, Jamie here, Head of ML at Altaeus. We're looking to validate inference economics and quality on our clinical summarization pipeline.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, Platform. I'll drive infra access and logs.
[00:21] Olivia: Olivia, Security — SOC 2 and data residency are our must-haves.
[00:25] Maya: Awesome. Arjun and Lena from my side — Arjun will lead the bench design, Lena will help with program ops.
[00:30] Arjun: Hi all. Quick note: we typically break the POC into a five to six week arc: week 0 access and kickoff, week 1 baseline benchmarks, weeks 2-4 optimizations and guardrail runs, week 4-5 mid-point review, then week 6 exec readout. But of course we'll flex to your schedule.
[00:50] Dana: That sounds good, our execs want the readout in early May if possible — puts pressure on a 6-week timeline.
[00:58] Maya: Good to know. If we start next week that fits. Today's main goals are: (1) confirm workload sizing and sample traces, (2) define success criteria (perf, cost, quality), (3) confirm access gating and timeline.
[01:18] Jamie: On workload — our pipeline sends about 8 RPS average for summarization, spikes to ~60 RPS during batch windows, average tokens per request ~320, 95th ~1,200. We can provide traces, though need to strip PHI.
[01:38] Samir: Correct, we'll scrub data; we'll provide histogram and a few representative payloads. Also we run in us-west-2 primarily.
[01:46] Olivia: Important: any logs or artifacts must be encrypted at rest with our KMS; we cannot allow model outputs to be stored outside our VPC without explicit controls.
[01:58] Arjun: Understood — for Redwood Private we can do VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; for hosted we have encryption at rest but we'd need an agreement for retention policies. Is Private required? Or do you want to try hosted first?
[02:15] Jamie: We'd prefer to start hosted to move quicker, but if compliance blocks it we can switch to Private. Security will decide.
[02:22] Olivia: We'll try hosted with strict retention and key controls, but we're likely to mandate Private for production. So POC flexibility is important.
[02:32] Maya: Cool. Now success criteria — we usually propose a combination: quality (ROUGE / task-specific pass rate > x%), latency (p95 token latency target), throughput (sustained RPS), and cost target (per-1M token cost or dollars per 1k requests). Arjun, can you sketch numbers?
[02:50] Arjun: From our prior pilots, a realistic POC threshold for you might be: latency p95 < 220ms TTI for conversational-length prompts (~320 tokens), end-to-end response wall time < 600ms for shorter flows — though summarization is longer so maybe p95 per-token is better metric. For throughput we should validate sustaining 60 RPS for short bursts with tail SLOs. Cost target — we'll estimate after we run baseline: aim to be cheaper than your current managed provider by 20% at parity quality.
[03:20] Jamie: Quality metric — our internal eval harness uses clinical ROUGE-L and a human pass rate. For POC we require human sampling with at least 80% pass on top-level acceptance and no critical hallucinations in the sample.
[03:33] Arjun: Ok let's codify: success criteria draft -> 1) Automated ROUGE-L >= X (we'll align exact number), 2) Human sample pass >= 80% on prioritized prompt set, 3) Latency p95 <= 300ms per-token (we'll calibrate for longer seqs), 4) Sustained throughput of 60 RPS for 10-minute windows with <5% error rate, 5) Cost per 1M tokens <= benchmark target (to be defined).
[04:05] Lena: We'll add deployment gates: access in 5 business days (if keys & VPC info provided), initial baseline completed within 10 business days after access, mid-point review scheduled ~3 weeks in, exec readout week 6.
[04:20] Samir: On access: we'll need a VPC peering window, firewall exceptions, and a short-lived AWS role for logs. Do you have a checklist?
[04:30] Arjun: Yes, we'll send an access checklist. For Private we request VPC peering + SG rules + SAML for SSO. For hosted we provide a secure endpoint and can do IP allowlist + customer-managed keys for artifacts.
[04:45] Olivia: Also need audit logs and retention policy — cannot retain request payloads beyond 30 days during POC unless redacted.
[04:55] Maya: We'll document retention policy in the runbook and mark where redaction is required.
[05:02] Jamie: Benchmarks: what exact tests will you run? Latency, throughput, cache hit validation, KV cache behavior, and quality regressions, correct?
[05:12] Arjun: Exactly: baseline cold starts, steady-state throughput, tail latency, and chunked long-sequence behavior. We'll also test quantized variants (8-bit) vs floats and note any quality drift. We'll run the eval harness you provide and also run our internal scoring scripts.
[05:30] Samir: For bench tooling, can you provide the scripts? We prefer to run inside our infra to reproduce.
[05:36] Arjun: We'll share load scripts (locust-based) and dockerized runner. We can run them from Redwood in your staging with tokens you provide, or you can run locally and share logs — whichever you prefer.
[05:50] Dana: We prefer to run in our staging to measure networking impact.
[05:54] Arjun: Great; then we need staging endpoint and test credentials — I'll follow up with an access guide.
[06:02] Maya: On the mid-point review — we'll present: baseline metrics, optimization actions taken, delta in cost, and risk areas. At exec readout we'll present final numbers, a recommended deployment path (hosted pilot vs dedicated), and a proposal for Dedicated capacity if you want predictable SLOs.
[06:22] Jamie: Can we include a fall-back plan? If the hosted latency is good but cost is higher, what's the path?
[06:28] Arjun: We'll show routing and quantization levers: smaller model variants for lower cost, batching strategies, and dedicated pools for lower per-token cost at high throughput. We'll include a compare table.
[06:41] Olivia: Security checklist again — SSO (SAML), customer KMS, VPC peering, minimal data persistence, and SOC 2 attestation. We may ask for an on-site audit for production later.
[06:55] Maya: Understood — we'll surface our SOC2 report and detail the data handling controls in the runbook.
[07:02] Jamie: Let's lock rough dates. If we get access by end of next week (Mar 27), staging runs week of Mar 30, baseline completed by Apr 7, mid-point Apr 20, exec readout May 4. Does that align?
[07:20] Lena: That gives 5-6 weeks. We can do May 4 for exec readout. I'll pencil that in and send calendar invites once dates confirmed.
[07:28] Samir: One concern — you mentioned quantization; we can't accept models that change accuracy materially. We need the eval harness to detect that.
[07:36] Arjun: We'll run A/B with float baseline and quantized; we'll expose regression alerting if metrics drop > 3% on ROUGE or human pass rate.
[07:48] Jamie: Sounds fair. Also can we measure token-level latency vs wall-clock? For long summaries the per-token metric helps.
[07:55] Arjun: Yep, we'll report both.
[08:00] (brief cross-talk about scheduling calendars)
[08:12] Maya: Ok, risks — what could block us: delayed access (VPC peering taking >10 business days), security denial of hosted option, or inability to share stripped traces. Those extend timeline.
[08:26] Samir: Our infra team sometimes requires change windows; I'll flag that.
[08:31] Olivia: We'll aim to provide a decision on hosted vs private by Mar 29 after reviewing docs.
[08:38] Dana: On stakeholders for readout — include Head of Ops and CFO for cost review.
[08:43] Maya: Good note — include them in invites.
[08:48] Arjun: Bench details — expected artifacts we'll deliver: baseline CSV metrics (latency percentiles, errors), cost model estimates, and sample outputs for human review. Also logs for debugging but redacted.
[09:02] Jamie: For human eval sample size what do you recommend?
[09:06] Arjun: For POC, 200 human-reviewed samples should be enough to get a signal; pick the highest-risk prompts.
[09:13] Jamie: We'll put together the set.
[09:16] Maya: Ok last piece — acceptance gates. We'll propose three gates: Access gate (can we run baseline?), Mid-point gate (sufficient progress and no critical regressions), Exec gate (meets thresholds or clear mitigation path). If any gate fails we'll document remediation and decide whether to extend or stop.
[09:35] Olivia: That sounds reasonable. If there are any unresolved security gaps at mid-point we may stop until they're remediated.
[09:41] Maya: Totally fine. We'll make the stop/extend criteria explicit in the runbook.
[09:47] (silence for a beat)
[09:50] Lena: I'll capture owners and dates now — Maya will send runbook by Mar 27, Samir to send traces Mar 30, Olivia to send required compliance docs Mar 29. Arjun will schedule the access workshop for week of Mar 30.
[10:06] Jamie: One quick technical question: for the KV cache behavior — long sessions in our UI reuse cached prefixes, how do you simulate that?
[10:16] Arjun: We'll run tests simulating prefix reuse and test cache hit rates; we'll also measure token savings and latency effects. If you have sample session traces that show prefix reuse patterns that helps.
[10:27] Samir: We'll add that to the traces.
[10:30] Maya: Any more questions?
[10:33] (small discussion about calendar times)
[10:40] Jamie: No more from me. This feels actionable.
[10:43] Olivia: We'll review docs and come back with hosted vs private decision by Mar 29.
[10:48] Maya: Great — recap of next steps: Maya send runbook + bench scripts (Mar 27), Samir provides traces (Mar 30), Arjun schedules access workshop (week of Mar 30), Olivia shares compliance requirements (Mar 29), and Lena schedules mid-point and exec readout (target May 4).
[11:05] All: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few mis-hearings on tech terms (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes shows as "KV cash"), names occasionally mapped to Speaker 1/2. We retained speaker attributions where possible and included some filler and cross-talk to keep it realistic.
